biography:
Rui Andrade's journey from the dusty karting tracks of Luanda, Angola, to the high-stakes world of international motorsport is a testament to sheer grit and determination. Growing up, racing wasn't a privilege; it was a dream fueled by stolen glimpses of Formula One on a crackling television. His first kart was pieced together from scrap, held together more by hope than hardware. One sweltering afternoon, a visiting European karting scout spotted Rui's raw talent amidst the chaos of a local race. That chance encounter led to a scholarship and a one-way ticket to Europe. 

Despite facing initial skepticism due to his background, Rui relentlessly climbed the ranks, leaving a trail of surprised rivals in his wake. A defining moment came in the Formula Renault series, where, after starting last due to a mechanical issue, he carved his way through the field to snatch victory on the final corner. His aggressive driving style and never-say-die attitude quickly garnered attention, earning him a spot in a prominent junior formula team. 

After a few years in Formula 2, Rui made the switch to endurance racing, initially seen as a step down by some, but Rui used it as an opportunity to showcase his versatility. He quickly adapted to the demands of long-distance racing, proving to be a reliable and remarkably quick driver. 

Now at what appears to be his peak, driving for the Black team, Rui is a formidable competitor, known for his relentless pursuit of victory and his unwavering commitment to pushing the limits.
drivingStyle: Andrade's driving style is characterized by controlled aggression. He's known for his late braking and daring overtakes, often threading the needle where others wouldn't dare. While some might perceive him as reckless, his approach is meticulously calculated. He possesses an uncanny ability to extract maximum performance from his tires, pushing them to the edge without crossing the line into premature degradation. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest, a testament to his mental fortitude and unwavering focus.

rivalries.name: Alessandro Rossi
rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision in Formula Renault that cost Rossi the championship.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: A fierce on-track battle for the lead in multiple endurance races, resulting in several near-miss incidents and accusations of unsportsmanlike conduct.

rivalries.name: Isabelle Dubois
rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities both on and off the track. Dubois, known for her calm and calculated approach, often criticizes Andrade's aggressive style, leading to tense exchanges in press conferences and team meetings.

quirks: Always wears the same faded wristband he got as a child in Angola.
Listens to Angolan Semba music at full volume exactly 30 minutes before every race.
Refuses to eat anything green on race day.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about heart. If you don't have the heart to fight, you don't belong on the track."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2028, after a nail-biting final stint where he defended the lead against relentless pressure from rivals, securing his team's first victory at the iconic race.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Spa 24 Hours in 2026 due to a mechanical failure, costing his team a guaranteed victory and leaving him visibly devastated.
